chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Our companions differ regarding the voluntary prayer; some of them pray four and forty, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me with which you act, how it is, so that I may act upon the like of it.' He said, 'I pray one and fifty.'

Then he said, 'Hold on!' And he counted with his hand: 'The midday is eight, and four after the Dhuhr, and four before the Asr, and two after the Maghrib, and two before the last Isha, and two after the Isha while seated, accounted as one while standing, and eight for the night prayer, and the Witr is three, and two of the Fajr, and the Obligatory ones are seventeen. So that is one and fifty.'
ai.seo_question: How many voluntary rak'at did Imam al-Rida (AS) perform daily and how were they distributed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi resolves the scholarly variance regarding the quantity of voluntary prayers by providing a precise, comprehensive count of fifty-one rak'at performed by Imam al-Rida (AS). It systematically categorizes these prayers into pre- and post-obligatory units, the night prayer (Tahajjud), and the Witr, offering a practical model for daily devotion. This detailed enumeration underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual consistency with spiritual flexibility in supererogatory acts.
